title: The Story of the Fisherman and the Demon

paragraphs.en: There was once a poor fisherman with his wife and three daughters. He cast his net four times daily but often struggled to find enough food. One night, after the morning prayer, he went out to fish at the seashore.
paragraphs.zh: 从前，有个贫穷的渔夫和他的妻子以及三个女儿。他每天出海捕鱼四次，但常常 struggle 以觅得足够的食物。一天清晨祷告后，他来到海边捕鱼。

paragraphs.en: He waded into the water, cast his net, and felt it grow heavier until he could no longer pull it in. Ashore, he tied the rope to a stake and dove back into the sea. After much effort, he managed to drag the net ashore.
paragraphs.zh: 他涉入水中，撒下渔网，感觉网越来越重，直到无法将其拉回岸边。上岸后，他将绳子系在一根木桩上，再次跳入海中。经过一番努力，终于把网拖上了岸。

paragraphs.en: Inside was a dead donkey that had torn the net.
paragraphs.zh: 里面是一头已经死去的驴子，它破坏了渔网。

paragraphs.en: The fisherman felt sad but recited verses about his labor:
paragraphs.zh: 渔夫感到悲伤，但还是念起了关于自己辛劳的诗句：

paragraphs.en: O you who brave the danger in the dark, Reduce your toil, for gain is not in work. Look at the fisherman who labors at his trade, As the stars in the night their orbits make, And deeply wades into the raging sea, Steadily gazing at the swelling net, Till he returns, pleased with his nightly catch, A fish whose mouth the hook of death has cut, And sells it to a man who sleeps the night, Safe from the cold and blessed with every wish.
paragraphs.zh: 你这勇敢的渔夫，夜色中冒险也不必太过劳累， 因为收获并不在于辛劳。看看那位渔民如何经营他的事业， 就像夜空中星辰按轨道运行，他深深踏入汹涌的大海， 凝视着渐渐鼓起的渔网，直到深夜归来，满心欢喜地展示那条被死神钓中的鱼。 然后将它卖给一个整夜安睡、无忧无虑的人。

paragraphs.en: Praised be the Lord who blesses and withholds: This casts the net, but that one eats the fish.
paragraphs.zh: 赞美那赐福与吝啬的主：撒网的是他，而捕鱼的却是另一个人。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad then paused. Her sister Dinarzad said, "Sister, what a lovely story!" Shahrazad replied, "Tomorrow night I shall tell you the rest, which is stranger and more wonderful, if the king spares me and lets me live!"
paragraphs.zh: 莎赫拉兹 then paused. 妹妹迪纳兹雅说道，“姐姐，多精彩的故事啊！” 莎赫拉兹雅回答道，“明天晚上我再给你讲剩下的部分，那部分内容更加奇异和奇妙，如果国王饶恕我让我活下去的话！”

paragraphs.en: The next night, Dinarzad urged her sister to continue: "If you are not sleepy, finish the fisherman’s story." Shahrazad agreed with pleasure.
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，迪纳兹达催促她的姐姐继续讲下去：“如果你不困的话，把渔夫的故事说完吧。”沙赫拉扎德愉快地答应了。

paragraphs.en: The fisherman, after reciting his verses, freed a snagged net and mended it. Upon returning to the water, he cast the net once more but found only mud and sand inside. Disappointed, he recited:
paragraphs.zh: 渔夫念完诗后，解开了缠住的网并修补好了。回到水边再次撒网，却发现网里只有淤泥和沙子。失望之余，他吟道：

paragraphs.en: O my tormenting fate, forbear, Or if you can’t, at least be fair. I went to seek, my daily bread, But they said to me it was dead. And neither luck nor industry Brought back my daily bread to me.
paragraphs.zh: 啊，折磨我的命运，求你克制一下吧，或者如果你不能，至少也公正一些。我曾去寻找每日的面包，但他们告诉我它已经不存在了。无论幸运还是努力，并没有为我带回每日的面包。

paragraphs.en: He then threw the jar away and washed his net. For a third time, he cast the net into the water but pulled up only broken pots, stones, bones, and refuse. Weeping, he recited:
paragraphs.zh: 他把罐子扔掉，清洗了渔网。第三次撒网入水，却只捞上来一些破瓷片、石块、骨头和垃圾。他边哭边念道：

paragraphs.en: Your livelihood is not in your own hands; Neither by writing nor by the pen you thrive. Your luck and your wages are by lot; Some lands are waste, and some are fertile lands. The wheel of fortune lowers the man of worth, Raising the base man who deserves to fall.
paragraphs.zh: 你的生计不由自己掌握，既非靠写作也非靠笔墨谋生。命运与报酬全凭抽签决定；有的土地荒芜，而有的则是肥沃之地。命运之轮让贤者屈居人下， 却将无能之辈高高举起。

paragraphs.en: Come then, O death, and end this worthless life, Where the ducks soar, while the falcons are bound to earth.
paragraphs.zh: 那么，死亡啊，请降临吧，终结这一无足轻重的生命，在此鸭子翱翔而鹰隼却被束缚于地面。

paragraphs.en: No wonder that you see the good man poor, While the vicious exalts in his estate. Our wages are alloted; 'tis our fate To search like birds for gleanings everywhere.
paragraphs.zh: 难怪你见那好人困顿，恶人却享福。我们的报酬早已注定，就像鸟儿四处分寻残余。

paragraphs.en: The fisherman looked up at the rising sun, realizing it was morning. Praying to God, he said, "O Lord, let the sea serve me as you did for Moses." After mending his net, he cast it into the sea and waited.
paragraphs.zh: 渔夫抬头望向冉冉升起的太阳，意识到已是清晨。他向上帝祈祷道：“主啊，请让大海像你曾经对摩西那样听我的吩咐。”修补好鱼网后，他把它抛进海里，然后耐心等待。

paragraphs.en: When he pulled, the net was so heavy he couldn't lift it. He shook it and found it stuck at the bottom. Saying a prayer, he took off his clothes and dove in to free the net.
paragraphs.zh: 当他拉扯时，网重得无法提起。他摇晃了几下，发现网被卡在了水底。于是他闭上眼默念了一番，脱掉衣服跳入水中，试图将网解救出来。

paragraphs.en: Finally, he managed to haul it ashore, feeling something heavy inside. Struggling with the net, he opened it to find a large brass jar sealed with a lead stopper marked by a seal ring.
paragraphs.zh: 终于，他费了好大的劲才把它拖上岸，感觉里面沉甸甸的。挣扎着打开渔网，只见里面有一个大号的铜罐子，封着一个铅制瓶塞，并且瓶塞上还刻有印记。

paragraphs.en: Excited, the fisherman thought he could sell the jar for two measures of wheat in the copper market. However, when he tried to move the jar, its weight and fullness made it impossible. Deciding to open the jar first, he took out his knife and scraped at the stopper.
paragraphs.zh: 兴奋之余，渔夫以为可以将瓶子拿到铜市场上卖两斗小麦。然而，当他试图移动瓶子时，却发现它异常沉重且鼓胀无比，根本无法挪动。于是他决定先打开瓶子，便掏出刀子，在瓶塞上刮了起来。

paragraphs.en: After much effort, he pried it loose and held the stopper in his mouth. Tilting the jar, he shook it but nothing came out, leaving him extremely surprised.
paragraphs.zh: 经过一番努力，他终于将瓶塞拔了出来，并含在嘴里。他倾斜着瓶子摇晃了几下，却什么也没有出来，这让他大感意外。

paragraphs.en: After a while, smoke began rising from the jar and spread over the earth. It rose so high that it reached the clouds, hiding the daylight. For a long time, the smoke kept rising until it took shape into a demon with feet on the ground and head in the clouds.
paragraphs.zh: 过了一会儿，烟从罐子里冒出来，弥漫在整个大地。它升得很高，直冲云霄，遮住了阳光。浓烟持续上升了很长时间，最终凝结成一个脚踏地面、头触云端的恶魔。

paragraphs.en: The demon had an eerie appearance: a tomb-like head, pincer-like fangs, a cave-like mouth, stone-like teeth, trumpet-like nostrils, shield-like ears, an alley-like throat, and lantern-like eyes.
paragraphs.zh: 恶魔的外观令人毛骨悚然：像坟墓般阴森的脸庞，钳子般的利齿，洞穴般的嘴巴，石头般的牙齿，号角般的鼻孔，盾牌般的耳朵，巷道般的咽喉，灯笼般的双眼。

paragraphs.en: Terrified, the fisherman saw the demon and his jaws locked together, his mouth going dry. The demon cried out, "O Solomon, prophet of God, forgive me. Never again will I disobey you or defy your command."
paragraphs.zh: 渔夫惊恐万分，只见恶魔张大嘴巴，合不拢嘴，口干舌燥。恶魔喊道：“所罗门，上帝的先知啊，请宽恕我。今后我再也不会违抗你的命令或挑战你的权威了。”

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad said, "Sister, what a strange and amazing story!"
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹默不作声。丁纳扎德说：“姐姐，这真是一个奇异而精彩的故事！”

paragraphs.en: The next night, in bed with King Shahrayar, Dinarzad urged, "Please, sister, finish the story of the fisherman." Shahrazad replied, "With pleasure."
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，与沙哈拉叶尔王同榻而眠时，丁纳扎德催促道：“妹妹，请你继续讲渔夫的故事吧。”莎赫拉兹德应道：“我很乐意。”

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad continued: When the fisherman heard the demon's words, he asked, "Demon, what are you saying? It has been over one thousand and eight hundred years since Solomon died. Why were you in this jar?"
paragraphs.zh: 沙赫拉扎德继续说道：当渔夫听到妖魔的话时，他问道：“妖魔，你这是什么意思？所罗门国王已经去世一千八百多年了，你怎么会在这只罐子里呢？”

paragraphs.en: The demon said, "Be glad!" The fisherman cried, "O happy day!" But the demon added, "You will soon be put to death."
paragraphs.zh: 恶魔说：“你应该高兴！”渔夫喊道：“多么幸福的一天啊！”但恶魔又补充道：“你很快就会被处死。”

paragraphs.en: The fisherman replied, "You deserve shame for such tidings. I freed you from the sea and brought you back to life—why kill me?"
paragraphs.zh: 渔夫回答说：“你这样的消息真是丢脸。我把你从海中救出，让你重获生机——为什么要杀我？”

paragraphs.en: The demon asked, "Make a wish!" The fisherman was happy and said, "What shall I wish?" The demon replied, "Tell me how you wish to die."
paragraphs.zh: 恶魔说道：“许个愿吧！”渔夫高兴地说：“我想要许什么愿？”恶魔回答道：“告诉我你希望自己以何种方式离世。”

paragraphs.en: The fisherman asked, "What is my crime? Is this my reward for freeing you?" The demon answered, "Fisherman, listen to my story.
paragraphs.zh: 渔夫问道：“我的罪是什么？我释放你，怎么会得到这样的回报？”妖怪回答说：“渔夫，请听我说我的故事。

paragraphs.en: Make it short; I am at my rope's end."
paragraphs.zh: “快点说吧，我已经迫不及待了。”

paragraphs.en: The demon spoke, "I am one of Solomon's rebellious demons who rebelled against his son, David’s descendant. I was captured by Asif ibn-Barkhiya and imprisoned in a brass jar sealed with God’s name. Solomon ordered his demons to throw me into the sea.
paragraphs.zh: 恶魔说道：“我是所罗门王反叛的妖魔之一，曾反抗大卫王的后裔。我被阿西夫·本-巴尔希亚捕获，并囚禁在一个封有上帝名号的铜罐中。所罗门命令他的妖魔将我投入大海。”

paragraphs.en: I remained there for four hundred years, promising wealth or kingship to anyone who freed me. No one did. Now you have set me free.
paragraphs.zh: 我在这里困了四百年，承诺只要有人把我解放出来，就能得到财富或是王位。可没有人做到这一点。现在你终于把我释放了。

paragraphs.en: Tell me how you wish to die."
paragraphs.zh: 告诉我你希望以怎样的方式离开这个世界。

paragraphs.en: The fisherman replied, "I didn't know what I was doing. I just found this jar and opened it out of curiosity."
paragraphs.zh: 渔夫回答说：“我当时也不知道在做什么，只是出于好奇打开了这个罐子。”

paragraphs.en: The demon growled, "You will pay for your curiosity. Choose your death now."
paragraphs.zh: 恶魔低吼道：“你的好奇心将付出代价。现在选择你的死法吧。”

paragraphs.en: When the fisherman heard the demon's words, he responded, "To God we belong and to Him we return. After all these years, with my bad luck, I had to set you free now. Forgive me, and God will grant you forgiveness.
paragraphs.zh: 渔夫听了魔鬼的话，脱口而出：“我们属于上帝，也将归于上帝。这么多年过去，倒霉的我如今只能放你出去了。求你原谅我，上帝也会宽恕你的。”

paragraphs.en: Destroy me, and God will inflict on you one who will destroy you." The demon replied, "It must be. Tell me how you wish to die."
paragraphs.zh: “毁了我，上帝就会降下一个敌人来毁灭你。”恶魔回答说，“那就这样吧。告诉我，你想以什么方式死去？”

paragraphs.en: The fisherman, certain of his fate, mourned and wept, saying, "O my children, may God not deprive us of each other." He then turned to the demon and said, "For God’s sake, release me as a reward for releasing you and delivering you from this jar." The demon retorted, "Your death is your reward for releasing me and letting me escape."
paragraphs.zh: 渔夫深知自己的命运，不禁悲从中来，泪如雨下，说道：“我的孩子们啊，但愿上帝不要将我们彼此分离。”随后他转向恶魔，哀求道：“求求你了，放我一马吧，作为回报，让我把你从这个罐子里救出来。”恶魔冷笑道：“你的死就是对你释放我的最好报偿，让你让我逃出生天。”

paragraphs.en: The fisherman argued, "I did you a good turn, and you are about to repay me with a bad one. How true is the sentiment of these lines:
paragraphs.zh: 渔夫争辩道：“我帮你忙在先，你却要报答我一个坏的。正如这两句诗所说：”

paragraphs.en: Our kindness they repaid with ugly deeds,
paragraphs.zh: 他们对我们的好意以丑恶的行为回报。

paragraphs.en: Upon my life, the deeds of men depraved.
paragraphs.zh: 天哪，人类的所作所为真是堕落至极。

paragraphs.en: He who the undeserving aids will meet
paragraphs.zh: 援助不配者者终将自食其果。

paragraphs.en: The fate of him who the hyena saved."
paragraphs.zh: 被土狼救下的那个人的命运。

paragraphs.en: The demon said, "Be brief, for as I have said, I must kill you." The fisherman thought to himself, "I am a human being, whom God has endowed with reason and thereby made superior to him. He may use his demonic wiles on me, but I will use my reason to deal with him."
paragraphs.zh: 恶魔说道：“言归正传，因为我已经说过，我必须杀了你。”渔夫心想：“我是人，上帝赋予了我理性，因此使我凌驾于他之上。他可以使用他的妖法对付我，但我将用我的理性来应对他。”

paragraphs.en: Then he asked the demon, "Must you kill me?"
paragraphs.zh: 然后他问那个恶魔，“你一定要杀我吗？”

paragraphs.en: When the demon replied, "I must," the fisherman said, "By the Almighty name that was engraved on the ring of Solomon the son of David, will you answer me truthfully if I ask you about something?" The demon was upset and said with a shudder, "Ask, and be brief!"
paragraphs.zh: 当妖怪回答说“我必须”时，渔夫说道：“凭着所罗门王大卫之子的戒指上刻的全能之名，如果你答应如实回答我的问题，你会回答吗？”妖怪听了这话显得很不悦，颤抖着说道：“问吧，快点！”

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad paused. Dinarzad then said, "Sister, what an amazing and lovely story!" Shahrazad replied, "What is this compared to the one I shall tell you tomorrow night if the king spares me and lets me live!
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫札德停下了口吻。迪纳札德 then 说道：“姐姐，这个故事真是奇妙又迷人！”沙赫札德回答道：“比起我明天晚上如果国王饶恕我不再杀我的那个故事，这根本不算什么！”

paragraphs.en: It will be even more amazing."
paragraphs.zh: 这将更加令人惊叹。

paragraphs.en: The fisherman said, "By the Almighty name, tell me whether you were truly inside this jar." The demon replied, "By the Almighty name, I was imprisoned in it." The fisherman retorted, "You are lying; this jar is too small for your hands and feet.
paragraphs.zh: 渔夫说道：“凭至高者的名义，告诉我你真的被关在这个罐子里吗？”妖怪回答道：“凭至高者的名义，我确实被囚禁在里面。”渔夫反驳道：“你在撒谎；这个罐子太小，容不下你的手脚。”

paragraphs.en: How could it fit your whole body?" The demon insisted, "By God, I was inside. Don’t you believe me?"
paragraphs.zh: “这怎么可能装得下你的 entire body？”恶魔坚持道，“天哪，我可是在里面呢。你不相信我吗？”

paragraphs.en: The fisherman remained skeptical. Suddenly, the demon shook himself and turned into smoke. The smoke rose over the sea, spread across the land, then gathered and slowly entered the jar.
paragraphs.zh: 渔夫仍持怀疑态度。突然，妖怪浑身一震，化作一团烟雾。这团烟雾升上天空，弥漫过海面和陆地，随后凝聚起来，缓缓进入了瓶子中。

paragraphs.en: When all the smoke disappeared, the demon shouted from within, "Fisherman, here I am in the jar. Do you believe me now?"
paragraphs.zh: 当烟雾完全消散，妖怪从罐子里喊道：“渔夫，我现在在罐子里。你现在相信我了吧？”

paragraphs.en: The fisherman quickly removed the sealed stopper from the jar and tightly placed it back on top. "Demon," he shouted, "tell me how you wish to die. I will throw you into this sea, build a house here, and warn any fisherman who comes that there is a demon inside who will kill them if they pull him out.
paragraphs.zh: 渔夫迅速取下封住瓶口的塞子，又紧紧地盖了回去。“妖怪，”他喊道，“告诉我你希望怎么死。我会把你扔进海里，在这里建一座房子，并警告任何前来打鱼的人，瓶子里有个妖怪，如果他们敢把瓶子打开，就会被杀死。”

paragraphs.en: You can choose your own method of death." The demon struggled but was unable to escape the seal of Solomon. Realizing he had been tricked, the demon pleaded, "Fisherman, don't do this!
paragraphs.zh: 你可以选择自己的死法。”恶魔挣扎着，却摆脱不开所罗门的封印。意识到自己上了当，恶魔哀求道：“渔夫，不要这样做！”

paragraphs.en: I was only joking."
paragraphs.zh: 我只是开个玩笑。

paragraphs.en: The fisherman retorted, "You are lying, you dirtiest and meanest of demons," and began rolling the jar towards the sea. The demon cried out, "No, no!" but the fisherman continued, "Yes, yes."
paragraphs.zh: 渔夫反驳道：“你这个最卑鄙无耻的妖魔，你在撒谎。”说着便将瓦罐朝着海里滚去。那妖魔喊道：“不，不！”但渔夫却坚持道：“是的，就是。”

paragraphs.en: In a submissive voice, the demon asked, "Fisherman, what do you intend to do?" The fisherman replied, "I will throw you into the sea again. You stayed there for eight hundred years last time; this time I'll keep you until Doomsday.
paragraphs.zh: 恶魔用一副屈服的语气问道：“渔夫，你想怎么办？”渔夫回答说：“我打算再把你扔回海里。上次你在那里待了八百年；这次我会一直留着你，直到世界末日。”

paragraphs.en: Haven't I warned you that if you spare me, God will spare you? If you destroy me, He will destroy you?"
paragraphs.zh: 我不是警告过你吗？如果你饶恕我，上帝也会饶恕你；如果你毁灭了我，他也必将毁灭你们。

paragraphs.en: The demon offered, "Fisherman, open the jar and I will reward you and make you rich." The fisherman dismissed him, saying, "You are lying. Your situation is like King David's and the sage Duban's."
paragraphs.zh: 妖怪提议：“渔夫，你打开瓶子，我会报答你，并让你变得富有。”渔夫不以为然地说：“你在说谎。你的处境就像大卫王和智者杜班的处境一样糟糕。”

paragraphs.en: The fisherman then recounted a story: "When Moses and his people fled Egypt, pursued by Pharaoh and his army, Moses parted the Red Sea with his staff, allowing them to cross safely while drowning their pursuers. In Islam, Moses is also a prophet."
paragraphs.zh: 渔夫接着讲述了一个故事：“当摩西和他的族人逃离埃及，法老及其军队紧追不舍时，摩西用权杖分开红海，让族人们安全渡过，而淹死了追赶者。在伊斯兰教中，摩西也是先知之一。”
